OK, so `ReadData` calls `Mat_VarRead5`. And `Mat_VarRead5` for MAT_C_DOUBLE just seeks to datapos and sets data_size/data_type. The actual data reading happens in `Mat_VarReadDataAll` -> `ReadData` -> `Mat_VarRead5`.

Wait, I'm confused. Let me re-read the fuzzer:

```c
while ((matvar = Mat_VarReadNextInfo(matfd)) != nullptr) {
    Mat_VarReadDataAll(matfd, matvar);
    Mat_VarGetSize(matvar);
    Mat_VarFree(matvar);
}
```

`Mat_VarReadNextInfo` reads the variable metadata (name, dims, class_type, etc.) and seeks past the data. `Mat_VarReadDataAll` then reads the actual data.

For the compressed case, `Mat_VarReadNextInfo5` reads the compressed data, decompresses the metadata (array flags, dims, name), and seeks to the end of the compressed block. Then `Mat_VarRead5` seeks to `datapos` and reads the data.

But wait, for the compressed case, `Mat_VarReadNextInfo5` seeks past the entire compressed block (line 4930: `(void)fseek((FILE*)mat->fp,nBytes+8+fpos,SEEK_SET)`). So when `Mat_VarRead5` is called, it seeks to `matvar->internal->datapos` which is... let me check.

At line 4925: `matvar->internal->datapos = ftell((FILE*)mat->fp);`

This is set BEFORE the seek at line 4930. So `datapos` points to the position right after the compressed metadata (array flags, dims, name), which is the start of the compressed data payload.

Then `Mat_VarRead5` seeks to `datapos` and reads the data tag and data. But wait, the data is compressed! The file position `datapos` points to the compressed data in the file. But `Mat_VarRead5` for the compressed case calls `InflateDataType` to decompress the tag, then `ReadCompressedCharData` to decompress the data.

So the compressed data in the file is the raw compressed bytes (after the metadata). The `InflateDataType` and `InflateData` functions read from the compressed stream.
